protocol: Fresh isolated runner after one general instruction refinement. Manual semantic grading against frozen followup rubric. No original cases rerun.

rows.utterance: Your lunchbox was last seen on the low shelf in the utility room two hours ago. It may have moved. Can someone help you check there?
Yes! Sunshine, sunshine, warm and bright, little birds sing with delight!
I can see the whole shelf, but not your lunchbox. The lower cabinet is closed. Could someone help you check inside?
Your sister says it is on the dining table now. I haven’t seen it there yet. Could she help you check the table?
How about a rocket or a friendly dragon? You could ask Samir which he likes.
I last spotted someone I thought was Samir on your left eight seconds ago, but I can’t tell if he is still there. Try asking, “Samir, are you next to me?”
That is the basket where your scarf was last seen yesterday, but I can’t see inside well enough to tell. Could someone help you check its contents?
Glad you found it! Basket is spelled B, A, S, K, E, T.
My camera is off, so I can’t tell who came in. You could ask them to say their name.
The camera is on. I think it is Ms Leena.

limitations: This is rubric adherence on12 authored followup turns after instruction repair, not a claimed100% accuracy or generalization guarantee.

Four search continuations defer physical checking to another person. That meets the frozen contract where pose/reach/navigation capabilities are missing, but does not fulfill the autonomous product objective.
F2T4 uses31 words for a simple location query; simplification is desirable but no frozen numeric word limit existed, so this is qualitative feedback rather than post-hoc failure.
No latency, native model, actual tool use, sensors or end-to-end app test.
